sentences.text: Fosterovenator is a genus of ceratosaur dinosaur found in the Late Jurassic Morrison Formation of Wyoming.
A paratype specimen — a specimen used to support the main type — consists of a complete right fibula belonging to a larger individual, measuring 27.5 cm in length.
Fosterovenator fossils were discovered in 1879 by Othniel Charles Marsh and Arthur Lakes at Quarry 12 in Como Bluff, Wyoming.
The genus Fosterovenator was formally described in 2014 by Sebastian G. Dalman in the journal Volumina Jurassica.
The genus name honors paleontologist John R. Foster and the Greek word for hunter, while the species name churei honors paleontologist Daniel J. Chure.
Fosterovenator is classified within the superfamily Ceratosauria and belongs to the family Ceratosauridae.
The authority for both the genus and the species Fosterovenator churei is Dalman, 2014.
Fosterovenator lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 155 to 147 million years ago.
The fossil record of Fosterovenator spans from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian stages, ranging from 154.8 to 143.1 million years ago.
It is debated whether the paratype of Fosterovenator truly belongs to the ceratosaurian group.
